title: Inverse image of etale abelian sheaves commutes with colimits
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes and $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on the categories of abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For every small category $I$ and every diagram $F:I\to\Ab(V_{\Et})$, $i\mapsto F_i$, with colimit $\varinjlim_iF_i$ in $\Ab(V_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the canonical morphism

$$
\varinjlim_i u^{-1}F_i\longrightarrow u^{-1}\bigl(\varinjlim_iF_i\bigr),
$$

induced by the morphisms $u^{-1}$ of the coprojections $F_i\to\varinjlim F_i$, is an isomorphism; that is, $u^{-1}$ preserves all small colimits.

source.place: Lemma 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact, line 3472), part (1), applied to the adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$; used in this form in literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, proof of Lemma 0A4B (line 18389: 'The functors $g^{-1}$ and $(g')^{-1}$ commute with arbitrary colimits (as left adjoints)')

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] the inverse image $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ is the left adjoint of the direct image $u_*:\Ab(U_{\Et})\to\Ab(V_{\Et})$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: there are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab(U_{\Et})}(u^{-1}G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Ab(V_{\Et})}(G,u_*F)$ natural in $G\in\Ab(V_{\Et})$ and $F\in\Ab(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$. This is an instance of the definition.

source.place: Definition 03Q0 (definition-inverse-image, line 4588): $f^{-1}:\textit{Ab}(Y_\etale)\to\textit{Ab}(X_\etale)$ is left adjoint to $f_*$, with the bijection $\Hom(f^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F)=\Hom(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F)$ functorial in both variables

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] with $\mathcal C=\Ab(V_{\Et})$, $\mathcal D=\Ab(U_{\Et})$, $L=u^{-1}$, $R=u_*$ (step 1) and the diagram $M=F:I\to\Ab(V_{\Et})$ with its colimit $(\varinjlim_iF_i,(\iota_i)_i)$: the cocone $(u^{-1}(\varinjlim_iF_i),(u^{-1}\iota_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto u^{-1}F_i$. The canonical morphism $c:\varinjlim_iu^{-1}F_i\to u^{-1}(\varinjlim_iF_i)$ is by definition [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] the unique morphism with $c\circ\iota'_i=u^{-1}\iota_i$ for all $i$, $\iota'_i$ the coprojections of the chosen colimit of $u^{-1}\circ F$. Since the target cocone is also a colimit, its universal property gives a unique $d$ with $d\circ u^{-1}\iota_i=\iota'_i$; then $d\circ c$ and $c\circ d$ are compatible with the coprojections, hence equal to the identities by the uniqueness clauses of the two colimits. So $c$ is an isomorphism, for every small $I$ and every $F$: $u^{-1}$ preserves all small colimits.
